proof.criterion: Every directory this layout puts on the issue volume is accounted for in the reclaim paragraph — on the delete list or in an exemption — and the claim is checkable against the renderer rather than asserted.

proof.observed: The renderer's set is cache, data, tmp, state/<role>, bun/install/cache (manifest.go:731-737, 758), the Go pair under /legion/go and uv's /legion/uv (podkind.go:194-196). All seven appear in the paragraph: five on the delete list, two in the exemptions below it. proof.criterion: The data home's exemption rests on a reason the code supports, and the state-class directories are attributed to the path that actually holds them.
proof.surface: podsafety.go's EnsureStateHome contract and this volume, read against the exemption sentence.
proof.observed: podsafety.go:137-140 places Oh My Pi's state-class directories — run/daemons, logs, browser-profiles, reports, terminal-sessions — under $XDG_STATE_HOME/omp, with the parenthesis 'sessions are data-class'. The volume agrees: /legion/scratch/state/<role>/omp exists for the roles that have run, and /legion/scratch/data is 4.0K. The exemption now says the state home holds those directories (as the paragraph already exempted it for) and that /legion/scratch/data is the shared XDG_DATA_HOME, the data-class directory of every tool a role runs, exempt because nothing re-derives it: a cache, a temporary directory and an install cache are rebuilt by the next build or install, where what a tool stores in its data home is gone when deleted. No size claim is made.
proof.negativeControl: The superseded sentence is the control, and it is what the code refutes: it said Oh My Pi puts its whole profile root under $XDG_DATA_HOME/omp, which would have made the data home the profile root and the state home redundant — contradicted by podsafety.go:137-140 and by the directories on this volume. The 4.0K reading is deliberately not used as evidence either way: these pods run the merge-base layout and are told no XDG_DATA_HOME at all.

proof.criterion: The between-turns rule states the limit of what the install block fixes, so the operator is not left believing a delete is safe under a running install.
proof.surface: The same paragraph, against the tester's round-18 measurements of the rendered block.
proof.command: read docs/kubernetes.md's between-turns sentence at this head
proof.observed: It says a lock whose inode is unlinked protects nothing, so the mutual exclusion is still lost under a delete mid-install (the tester measured B entering at 886.599 while A was inside until 888.599, against a serialised control), and that what each attempt's mkdir and non-directory removal buys is that the damage stops at that install rather than leaving a regular file that fails every later installing launch until a person clears it.
proof.negativeControl: The tester ran this head's block from an already-poisoned path: exit 0, where the old block from the same fixture exits 1 at `mkdir: File exists`, and this head's block with only the `rm -f` guard removed fails the regular-file case again.

filesChanged: docs/kubernetes.md — /legion/scratch/data exempted with a reason the code supports, the state-class directories attributed to the per-role state home, no size claim, the completeness claim made enumerable, and the between-turns sentence given the limit of what the install block fixes.
trickyParts: The data home is exempt because nothing re-derives it, not because Oh My Pi's profile root lives there. $XDG_STATE_HOME/omp holds the state-class directories (podsafety.go:137-140); the data home is the data-class one. Anyone editing this paragraph again should read those four lines rather than the paragraph's own history.
discoveredComplexity: Four rounds in a row on one paragraph, each a sentence true of something other than what it described. The last one is the sharpest and it was the architect's: it ruled the exemption and supplied its reason, and the reason — the omp profile root under $XDG_DATA_HOME — was the one clause nobody derived, because it came from the role whose rulings the others have no standing to doubt. My enumeration control caught the structure (is every rendered path accounted for) and could not catch a false reason attached to a correctly-exempted path. A claim's structure and a claim's grounds need separate checks.

What finally made the completeness claim hold was its form rather than more care: 'accounts for every directory this layout creates, either on its delete list or in the two exemptions below it' is checkable by a seven-line loop, where 'names the directories this layout creates' could only be asserted. A prose claim that cannot be mechanically enumerated against the code it describes will drift again, however carefully it is written.
